svg.aria-label: Four steps. Node A 1001 and key 1110 are 0111, or 7, apart by XOR distance, and a smaller XOR distance means closer in the ID space. Node A keeps a routing table of known peers grouped by distance ranges 1, 2 to 3, 4 to 7 and 8 to 15. To find target key 1110, Node A queries Peer 1 at 1010, then Peer 2 at 1100 and Peer 3 at 1110, each step closer to the target. The lookup converges on Peer 3, whose ID, 1110, is closest to the target
svg.text: Kademlia DHT: XOR distance and peer lookup
Distance is the XOR of two IDs, and each lookup step asks peers that are closer to the target.
